sources.title: Kant, Beobachtungen über das Gefühl des Schönen und Erhabenen
sources.location: Third section, paragraphs contrasting female and male understanding
sources.purpose: The author's own usage supports reading the conventional beautiful-sex designation as referring to women. It does not establish the truth of the author's gender claims.

decisions: Keep the class referred to separate from the aesthetic description used as a designation.
The entire included class must satisfy the selected property, not merely some of its members.
Read the guardians collectively as covering the relevant people, allowing different guardians for different people.
Distinguish earlier assumption of a supervisory role from current possession of it and from present causal activity.
Attribute the causal claim to the author; do not endorse its gender generalization, actual danger, beauty or real-world causal truth.
remaining: A constructive account of sex classification and aesthetic evaluation is not yet supplied by the new primitive meaning conventions.
The pronoun scope and collective reading remain interpretations, not uniquely established readings.
The evaluative force of gutigst and the focal contributions of schon and auch remain unrepresented.
The following examples must supply the causal mechanism of the guardians' activity.
The 1784 facsimile has not been checked in this change.
